findings.description: The eviction loop compares len(self._keys_by_country), the number of distinct countries, with max_entries, not the number of cached entries. The cache therefore grows without bound: with 4096 as the limit, millions of postal codes within a few countries are never evicted. Memory use is unbounded, and the max_entries guarantee in the docstring is broken. The stats 'size' and 'evictions' are also misleading as a result.
findings.title: Capacity check counts countries instead of entries

findings.description: clear() empties the entries and the country index but leaves the hit, miss and eviction counters unchanged. This is a minor inconsistency, and it is arguably intentional.
findings.title: clear() does not reset statistics

findings.description: source.replace_country runs before calculator.rates_changed and without the cache lock. A concurrent get() can load the old or new table between the two calls, and the loader does not run under any lock shared with the source. A lookup that loads the new rate is harmless. A lookup that has just read the old table, however, can store the stale rate after the invalidation has run. That stale rate then stays cached for up to the TTL.
findings.suggestion: Do the replace and the invalidate under a single lock shared with the cache loader, or invalidate again after the replace.
findings.title: Table replacement and cache invalidation are not atomic
